# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 58 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 58 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_058_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter integrates the fasting theme (from ch. 54) with the conclusion of the vineyard parable. Hermas's practical instruction is that a fast must be combined with almsgiving: save the food you would have eaten and give it to those in need. This alms-integrated fast mirrors the "true fast" tradition in Isaiah 58:6-7 ("share your bread with the hungry").

The "ninth hour" (*hōra enatē*) corresponds to approximately 3:00 PM; this was the customary breaking-fast time in early Christianity (cf. Acts 10:30 — Cornelius praying at the ninth hour). The fast in question is the *statio* (Wednesday/Friday), mentioned in ch. 54.

The closing beatitude in 58:3 ("all who hear these words and observe them shall be blessed") is a characteristic prophetic formula — similar to Revelation 1:3.

EMET's "the service performed in this way is beautiful and joyful" and LOGOS's "beautiful and rejoicing" both render *kalos kai hilaros*. SOPHIA uses "beautiful and joyful" — "rejoicing" (LOGOS) is unusual for an adjective.

---

## Similitude 5, Part 4 — True Fasting and Almsgiving

**58:1** "Lord," I said, "I should also like to learn what the fasting means. How should we fast?" "Listen," he said. "The fast that you are to observe is this: when you fast on the appointed days, take no food at all until the ninth hour. But the foods that you would have eaten on that day, eat them after the ninth hour. And whatever is saved from your foods, give it to a widow, or an orphan, or to someone in need. So you humble yourself, in order that the one who receives may be filled from your act of humbling, and may pray to the Lord on your behalf."

**58:2** "If therefore you accomplish this fast as I have explained, your sacrifice will be acceptable before God, and this fast will be recorded; and the service performed in this way is beautiful and joyful and acceptable to the Lord."

**58:3** "These things you shall observe with your children and with all your household. And when you observe them, you shall be blessed. And all who hear these words and observe them shall be blessed; and whatever they ask of the Lord, they shall receive."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
